question.text: This northern neighbor of Germany lies on the Jutland peninsula. It also controls Greenland.
question.clue: This country lost a personal union with a nearby country in the 1814 Treaty of Kiel.

swap.leadin: The continent of Europe is home to many notable seas of the world.
swap.text: This sea in eastern Europe names the region containing Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia. Stockholm, Sweden, lies on the shores of this sea.
swap.clue: Dominion over this sea shifted east after the Treaty of Nystad.

question.leadin: The author of the Prose Edda, Snorri Sturluson, was a law speaker of a parliament in this country.
question.text: Name this country home to the Althing, so-named to trick people to move to Greenland.
question.clue: A period of internal clan violence in this country is called the Age of the Sturlungs, and involved this country's great writer of sagas, Snorri Sturluson.

swap.text: This Norwegian terrorist set off a car bomb in Oslo and carried out a mass shooting in Utoya, which he claimed to do in order to fight against the forces of Islam and multiculturalism.
swap.clue: First, name this right-wing extremist who was also responsible for the Utoya massacre, in which he opened fire on a crowd, killing 69 and injuring 66 at an AUF summer camp.

question.leadin: This monarch appointed the chancellor Axel Oxenstierna, who negotiated the Truce of Altmark with Poland on this monarch's behalf.
question.text: Name this Swedish king whose victory over the forces of the Count of Tilly at the Battle of Breitenfeld preceded his death at the Battle of Lutzen.
question.clue: In addition to ending the Kalmar War, one military rival to this person employed an elector named Maximilian I that died with him at Ingolstadt after losing to the numerically superior force of this ruler at the Battle of the Rain.

swap.text: This war between Finland and the Soviet Union resumed when Finland joined Germany in Operation Barbarossa and became the only democracy to fight with the Axis in World War II.
swap.clue: After serving as prime minister during an earlier conflict, Risto Ryti served as president during this conflict, in which one side aimed to annex East Karelia.

question.leadin: This leader was killed instantly by a shot to the head during the Siege of Fredriksten.
question.text: Name this monarch who ruled Sweden from 1697 to 1718.
question.answerHtml: Charles XII of Sweden [accept Carl XII; accept Carolus Rex]
question.clue: In one campaign, this man installed Stanis? aw Leszczy?

swap.text: Due to its ties to Poland, Saxony became embroiled in this long and destructive European conflict of the early eighteenth century. The power of Sweden began to decline after this war's Battle of Poltava.
swap.answerHtml: the Great Northern War [prompt on just "Northern War"]
swap.clue: During this war, one side relieved a siege during a snowstorm at the Battle of Narva.

question.text: Mannerheim's fortifications along the Karelian Isthmus, unsurprisingly dubbed the Mannerheim Line, enabled Finland to resist Soviet assault during the namesake season of 1939-1940. Afterwards, Mannerhim expanded his work to include the Salpa Line.
question.clue: The invading side was expelled from the League of Nations as a result, and a major goal of the war was to cut off Germany's supply of iron ore.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about Nazi collaborationist governments.
swap.text: The Nazis also replaced Johann Nygaardsvold with this leader of the Nasjonal Samling party, who governed with Josef Terboven.
swap.clue: This man was appointed Commander of the Order of the British Empire for his humanitarian works, which included a stint in the Ukraine trying to help alleviate a famine there in 1921 undertaken at the behest of mountain climbing-humanitarian Fridtjof Nansen.

question.text: This Norwegian claim, located between the British and Australian claims at 20 degrees West and around 44 degrees East, was named by Roald Amundsen after the wife of King Haakon VII.
question.clue: The Prime Meridian also passes through this Antarctic region. Claimed by Norway, this region is named for the wife of King Haakon VII ["the seventh"], who reigned from 1905 to 1957, and who was also the daughter of King Edward VII ["the seventh"] of Great Britain.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a northern European "Brave Little Democracy's" effort against Soviet Aggression in World War II.
swap.text: The Soviets' poor performance during the first stages of the Winter War was largely caused by this array of fortifications named after the Finnish commander-in-chief.
swap.clue: Reinforced concrete and protection plates were dropped from this due to a rise in the price of steel, and parts of it were simply strategically placed mounds of soil known as "slope cuts."

question.text: Due to skepticism over Henson's voyage, the first undisputed expedition to the North Pole was led by this Norwegian explorer, the first to reach the South Pole and traverse the Northwest Passage.
question.clue: This person led the crew that disappeared searching for the airship Italia and was the first to successfully navigate the North-west Passage in a boat, the Gjoa .

swap.text: The name of this Norwegian archipelago means "cold shores," and its three inhabited islands are Spitzbergen, Bear Island, and Hopen.
swap.clue: This Norwegian territory's namesake treaty regulates commercial and military activities. This Arctic archipelago is home to one of the largest seed banks in the world -- the Global Seed Vault.

question.leadin: Some sagas claim this man blinded Byzantine ruler Michael V.
question.text: Name this Norse king who invaded England and won the Battle of Fulford, but was slain in another battle the same year while fighting alongside Tostig, the rogue former Earl of Northumbria.
question.answerHtml: Harald Hardrada [or Harald Sigurdsson; or Harald III; prompt on Harald]
question.clue: This man married the daughter of Yaroslav the Wise, Elisiv of Kiev, on his return from Constantinople.

swap.leadin: This ship was salvaged in 1961, over 300 years after sinking on its maiden voyage.
swap.text: Name this ship, now housed at a namesake museum in Stockholm. This ship shares its name with the dynasty of its commissioner, who was advised by Axel Oxenstierna.
swap.clue: A queen from this royal house abdicated after converting to Catholicism and housed Descartes in his final years.

question.text: For Frederick I's rule and some years afterwards the riksdag was dominated by these two political parties, one of which assumed control of parliament in 1738 before giving way to the other in 1765.

swap.text: In this early battle of the Winter War, Russian troops on the Raate and Juntusranta roads were easy prey for defenders under Colonel Hjalmar Siilasvuo. Of the 44,000 in the Russian 44th, only 5,000 made it back to Russia.
swap.clue: The earlier Winter War saw the Finns decisively beat the Russians nearby the Gulf of Bothnia at this battle. Hjalmar Sililasvuo led Finnish forces here, defeating General Alexey Vinogradov and General Ivan Dashitsev.

question.text: Following the Battle of Poltava, Lewanhaupt and Charles adandoned everything leading to this time period of Norwegian history in which the Russians decimated the population of Norway.
question.answerHtml: The Greater Wrath [accept: isoviha from Will Alston; accept The Great Discord]

swap.leadin: He had to deal with revolts in Dalarna and one led by Nils Dacke, and at the Diet of Vasteras, he confiscated the property of Sweden's Catholic Church.
swap.text: Name this founder of the Vasa dynasty who signed the Treaty of Malmo with Christian II, thus relieving Sweden of Denmark's rule in the Kalmar Union.
